1.
Learned A.G.A. has informed that the notice to the informant has been served on 27.08.2024.

2. Heard Sri Yashpal Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Anit Kumar Shukla, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.233 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C., 3/4 POCSO Act and 3(2)5 SC/ST Act, Police Station Ghatampur, District Kanpur Nagar, during the pendency of trial.

1 PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The FIR was instituted against the applicant on the suspicion that he along with other family members is stated to have enticed away the two minor daughters of the informant on 12.05.2024 at about 11:00 a.m.

sentences.text: Another daughter of the neighbour was also found missing since then.

5. It is also mentioned in the FIR that the said daughters had earlier on also left the house without informing him and he was very unhappy with the said act and had also expressed his unwillingness to keep them in his house.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
6. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
7.

The statements of the two victims have been recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and they have categorically stated that they had gone with the applicant all the way to Indore in a bus and then to Delhi and were dropped later on at Kanpur by the applicant.
They have not levelled any kind of allegations against the applicant.

8. The third victim, who is stated to be aged about 20 years in the FIR, has stated in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that she was 17 years old and the applicant had abducted her and raped her by taking her to several places.
9. The victim has not uttered a single word of having raised any alarm during the said travelling with the applicant to several places.
10. The medical report does not support the prosecution story.
11. Even the factum that the two girls had gone with the applicant stands corroborated by her statement.
12. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
13. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 18.05.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/INFORMANT:
14.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

2 CONCLUSION:
15.
?The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

16. ?A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. ?Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
18. ?Learned A.G.A. could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
19. ?It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A.
20.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

21. Let the applicant- Deepak Thakur Urf Naveen Kumar involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
